lesson.lesson_summary: Learn what parts of speech are, why words belong to different groups, and how they help us build meaningful sentences.

learning_objectives.description: Understand what parts of speech are.
Understand that words can be grouped according to their grammatical behaviour.
Understand that words perform different jobs in sentences.
Recognise that grammatical categories help words work together to create meaningful sentences.
Understand that a word's grammatical category depends on how it is used.

content.text: Look around you. You see a book, a chair and a window. You can say, "I read a book." Every sentence is made using words.

examples.explanation: This short sentence uses four words to share one complete idea.

content.text: Not all words do the same job. Some name people or things. Some show actions. Others describe or connect words.

examples.explanation: "Girl" names a person, "happy" describes her, and "dances" tells us what she does.

pages.title: Meet the Word Teams

content.text: Parts of speech are groups of words based on how they work in language. Each group has its own grammatical role.
Think of them as different teams. Each team has a different job.

pages.key_takeaway: Parts of speech are grammatical word groups.

pages.title: Words Belong to Groups

content.text: Words can be grouped by their grammar. For example, words that name people, places or things belong to one group. Words that express actions belong to another.

examples.explanation: "Dogs" names animals. "Bark" tells us what they do.

pages.key_takeaway: Words are grouped by their grammatical behaviour.

pages.title: Words Work Together

content.text: Words join together to make sentences. Their different grammatical jobs help us understand who or what we are talking about and what is happening.

examples.explanation: "Brother" tells us who we mean. "Plays" tells us the action. "Football" tells us what he plays.

pages.key_takeaway: Words work together to express ideas.

content.text: Grammar helps words work together in an understandable order. Changing a word or its position can change the meaning or make a sentence unclear.

examples.explanation: The sentence tells us who did the chasing and who was chased.

pages.title: A Word Can Change Its Job

content.text: A word does not always belong to the same grammatical group. Its role can change when we use it differently in a sentence.

examples.sentence: I drink water. Please water the plant.
examples.explanation: In the first sentence, "water" names something. In the second, "water" describes an action.

pages.key_takeaway: A word's use helps determine its grammatical category.

pages.title: What Have You Learned?

items: Parts of speech are groups of words.
A word's grammatical category can depend on its use.

pages.key_takeaway: Parts of speech help us understand how words work.

questions.question: What are parts of speech?

options.text: Groups of words based on their grammatical roles
Groups of sentences based on their length

questions.explanation: Parts of speech group words according to how they work in language.

questions.question: In "The baby cries", which word tells us the action?
questions.explanation: "Cries" tells us what the baby does.

questions.question: A word can have different grammatical roles in different sentences.
questions.explanation: The word "water" names something in one sentence and expresses an action in another.

questions.question: Why do words work together in a sentence?

options.text: To make all words sound alike

questions.explanation: Words combine according to grammatical patterns to communicate meaningful ideas.
